sections.what_happened: A Board of Peace official says up to 500 Moroccan troops are training for the Gaza force; the Board is seeking greater Israeli cooperation after next week's elections, noting water/sewage projects and a proposed ISF base near the Yellow Line are delayed by outstanding Israeli approvals. Netanyahu reiterated Israel will not permit Gaza's reconstruction until Hamas is disarmed and Gaza demilitarized — except the 'Emirati bubble' near Israel's security zone. Nikolay Mladenov (Board high representative for Gaza) held 'constructive and detailed' talks with Netanyahu on a disarmament deal; Hamas says it remains committed to phase-two implementation. Bonikbarta relays claim that 1,250 people were killed in Israeli attacks since the October ceasefire — attributed only.
sections.what_verified: Board of Peace statements are primary; Times of Israel liveblog is a credible relay.
sections.what_disputed: The '1,250 killed since ceasefire' figure has no named primary source in the relay — do not use without verification. 'Since the ceasefire' framing is contested by the endtime.com item claiming Netanyahu ordered strikes after IDF fire.
sections.why_matters: The 'peace' is now run from a boardroom: 500 Moroccan troops training for Gaza, a Trump-chaired Board pressing Israel to disarm Hamas, and Netanyahu's one exception — the 'Emirati bubble.' Who actually governs Gaza now?
sections.context: Background: Gaza/Board of Peace update (extends 2100-03): up to 500 Moroccan troops training for Gaza force; Netanyahu 'Emirati bubble' comment

totw_analysis: Our read: The 'peace' is now run from a boardroom: 500 Moroccan troops training for Gaza, a Trump-chaired Board pressing Israel to disarm Hamas, and Netanyahu's one exception — the 'Emirati bubble.' Who actually governs Gaza now? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Peace plan or occupation management? Is the Board of Peace building a Palestinian future — or an internationally supervised Israeli security envelope?
